feb26.summary: Unsigned letter from London to Johann Georg von Ilten, Hanoverian lieutenant-general with the Pragmatic Army. The French cipher passage approves Du Pontpietin's instructions to Lieutenant-General Sommerfeldt about forage and asks that the troops eat up the forage in their quarters so the French find nothing if they quarter there after them.
feb26.en:
As regards the instructions which Monsieur the General Du Pontpietin has given to Monsieur the Lieutenant-General
von Sommerfeldt with regard to forage, they too are approved, as I have orders to state, just as there was no doubt of
the care that would be taken to continue always to keep good and exact discipline in that country. Nevertheless it is
wished that the troops consume, with r[?] the same good discipline, what forage there is in those quarters, so that
nothing of it remains if the French should take a fancy to take up quarters there after you in that country, so that
they would find there neither forage nor anything of what would be necessary for the subsistence of the troops. You
will make use of this last point according to your usual prudence.

mar29.summary: German letter from Ernst von Steinberg to Ilten with three code runs: it encloses an extract of the instruction just sent to Lord Stair, to be used with the utmost secrecy among His Majesty's German generals. A contemporary worksheet (p. 121) glosses the groups, partly wrongly.
mar29.en:
⟨By His Royal Majesty's most gracious command I am not only to enclose herewith a copy of the Royal rescript going
today to General du Pontpietin, but also to add, for information, an⟩ extract of the instruction which has just been
sent to My Lord Stair, ⟨and to this end, that Your Excellency⟩, though with the utmost care for secrecy, ⟨may make use
of it with His Royal Majesty's⟩ German generals.

snip.cap: The unsigned London letter of 15/26 February 1743: German clear text, then the code that no one deciphered
snip.credit: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Bibliothek Hannover, Ms XXIII 1234:29,2 p. 73, via the GWLB digital library

system: Hanoverian French syllabic nomenclator of 863 numbered groups (blanks and 864-1000 are nulls), with homophones, officers' and place names, and control groups 'annulle' / 'repete la precedente'.
